About Me

Turning complexity into clarity.
Helping you move forward with confidence.

I spent years in project management and consulting, where the work was to take something complicated and make it understandable — then help people move forward with confidence. That's still the job. Only the subject has changed.

What I kept noticing was how many hardworking families had never had one honest conversation about protecting what they were building. Not because they weren't interested. Because no one had ever explained it in a way that respected their time or their intelligence.

So that's what I do now. I sit down with individuals, families, and business owners, I ask a lot of questions, and I explain how life insurance actually works — the trade-offs included. Some people move forward. Some decide it isn't the right season. Both are fine outcomes.

No scripts, no pressure, no jargon. If I don't know something, I'll tell you and find out. If a product isn't a fit for your situation, I'll say so.

My Philosophy

Protection starts with understanding what matters.

Before discussing coverage, we start with your life — your family, responsibilities, existing coverage, budget, and what you want to protect. Then we can discuss life insurance options for your consideration.

Understanding comes first

You should be able to explain your own coverage to someone else. If you can't, we haven't finished the conversation.

Questions are the work

The most useful part of a first conversation is usually the questions you hadn't thought to ask yet.

No is a complete answer

Deciding not to move forward is a legitimate outcome. The door stays open either way.

FAQs

A few things people often ask.

Do I need to know what type of life insurance I want before we talk?
No. The first conversation is about understanding your responsibilities, existing coverage, priorities, and questions. You do not need to choose a product in advance.
Does a conversation mean I have to apply?
No. The first conversation is complimentary and educational. If you decide to explore an application, that is a separate step and is subject to underwriting and product availability.
Can I have life insurance through work and still consider separate coverage?
Yes. Workplace coverage and individually owned coverage can serve different purposes. It can be useful to review what you already have, how long it lasts, and whether it changes if you leave your employer.
Can health affect eligibility or premiums?
Yes. Age, health, coverage amount, and other underwriting factors may affect eligibility and cost. Requirements vary by carrier, policy, state, and applicant.
